notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Morrowind starts on every console again: 2.39.6 shipped its engine without
four libraries a stock console does not have. The engine now carries
everything it needs and no longer installs packages on first launch.

The PS2 pause menu gains Eject disc, Memory cards (pick, eject or create a
card per slot for the session) and Press the ANALOG button, and its
Performance rows no longer leave the paused game on top of the menu.

The volume bar draws with clean rounded corners over a game. The overlay's
RAM row shows the speed your overclock installed rather than the step it
happened to sample. Clean Dark and Clean Light show the focus ring on the
CPU and GPU pills. "Reboot to..." shows icons for every hekate entry.

DraStic binds the pad your controller setup was captured for, and controller
setup asks you to confirm a stick that reads the opposite way. The DS and 3DS
stick pointer no longer vanishes while you hold the stick; docked dual-screen
3DS keeps it on the bottom screen.

The Updates tab and update notification scroll with the pad. Zipped multi-disc
imports show "Converting" instead of "Queued" while each disc packs. A serial
or title ID shows on a game's page. The volume buttons repair themselves when
a boot leaves them unreadable. A sleep log records each sleep with battery
before and after. The RAM tuner refuses to start while docked again. Game Gear
and Virtual Boy tabs are new and untested on hardware.

Display and Sound is five short pages instead of one long scroll, the
Settings tabs wrap so none hide off the edge, and the game page folds its
rarely used rows into More with Performance settings grouped for drilling
into. The PS2 in-game Game menu splits into Saves and Disc and hardware.
Clean Light applies everywhere, including the game page and the remap
screen, which were unreadable on it. Descriptions are shorter, lists fade
where more content follows, and docked modals fit 1080p.

Controllers no longer go dead after days of uptime: the device manager was
losing track of its helper processes on this kernel until it stopped handling
new devices. A one-line fix is installed at boot.

The launcher recovers from a crashed page: it reloads within seconds, and
restarts itself if the reload does not hold, instead of sitting on a black
screen.

Colours have Lightness and Vividness sliders and a brown preset. Backgrounds
have a None option and an opacity slider; clean themes default to none. Home
screen overlays get toggles for IP, clocks and time. The game page puts
Compatibility at the top level, drops Play Online and one-item More menus,
and shows Rumble only on consoles that have it. RetroAchievements can be
sorted by points or by how close they are. Performance settings were
regrouped (Overclock, RetroArch, Advanced, ARMSX2 Advanced). Ports and Apps
hides unused tiles until you add them with Add ports/apps. The in-game
Performance overlay row can turn the HUD back on.

stable.notes:
You can now choose whether this console takes every update or only stable ones.

Settings, Updates asks what you would like. Stable releases only is the default
and is what you have effectively been on until now. Latest Updates also takes
the builds released between stable ones, which carry new features first and are
more likely to have rough edges. You can change it whenever you like.

Wii U community packs now actually apply. Turning on a pack such as Resolution
or Shadow Resolution and choosing a value did nothing in game, and reopening the
menu could show the option named as an unreadable tag. The console was writing
your choice in a shape Cemu does not read, so the pack switched on with no value
behind it. Your existing choices are not lost: a pack that lost its value falls
back to its own default and sticks the next time you pick one.

On the Uploading tab, the Remove button on a parked upload can now be reached
with a controller. Press down from the tab bar to step onto it, and again to
confirm. Until now that button could only be pressed from the console's :8097
page in a browser.
